title: The bell's alert count is kept per browser, so the same alerts count as new again on every other device
what: Opening the bell marks the gym's alerts seen only in this browser. The owner's phone, a second laptop or a staff member's computer still counts the same alerts as new, and the alert push sent while the panel is closed does not know they were seen.
expected: Seen alerts stop counting as new for that person on every device, or the bell says the count is for this device only.
who: owners and staff who use the panel on more than one device
how_often: every time someone uses a second device
fix_line: Keep the bell's last-seen time on the server per person and read it on every device

title: Set-up steps ticked by hand and the last backup day are remembered only in one browser
what: The 'Set up your gym' steps the owner ticks by hand (and 'hide this list') and the 'last downloaded a backup' day are kept in this browser only. On the owner's phone or a new computer the ring shows unfinished steps again and the backup card says no backup was taken.
expected: Steps and the backup day follow the gym, so every device shows the same progress and the real last backup.
who: owners using more than one device
how_often: every time the owner opens the panel on another device
fix_line: Save these marks with the gym on the server

title: Some Save buttons go grey with no line saying everything is already saved
what: On the friend free-days card and the gym timings page the Save button is greyed out while nothing has changed, with no words beside it. On the alert-timing card the 'Saved' words show only right after a save in this visit, so on opening the page the grey button stands alone. Other pages say 'No changes to save' or 'All changes saved'.
expected: Next to every greyed Save button, a short line says it is already saved.
fix_line: Add the same 'No changes to save' line the busy-machines page uses

title: Messages, trainer questions and workout reports are deleted only when someone next opens them, not on the day the privacy notice promises
what: The privacy notice says member messages and trainer questions are kept 180 days and a sent workout report 30 days. In code the old ones are removed only when the member or the gym next opens that list. The nightly clean-up does not touch them. If a member stops using the app and the gym never opens that list again (or the gym stops using MettleUp), the data stays with no end date.
expected: A nightly job deletes them on time for every gym, whether or not anyone opens the list.
who: members of gyms that go quiet or leave
how_often: whenever neither side opens the list for longer than the promised time
fix_line: Add these three deletions to the nightly clean-up for all gyms

title: 'Every look by support is recorded' has no record for looks made straight in the database
what: The privacy notice promises that every look MettleUp support takes at a gym's records is recorded and shown to the owner. Looks through HQ are recorded, but a look made through the database's own dashboard, table editor or a direct login goes through no app code, and no migration in this folder turns on a database-level audit (no audit setting, no job that pulls the database's logs).
expected: Either a database-level record of every direct read of gym tables, or the notice limits the promise to looks made through HQ.
proof: code-read (searched every migration in this folder for an audit setting: none)
who: members and owners relying on the promise
how_often: every time someone opens the database directly
fix_line: Turn on a database audit for reads of gym tables, or narrow the notice wording

title: Phone pop-ups to members leave no record the owner can open of who got one and who did not
what: Every minute the server sends the gym's messages, offers and trainer replies as phone pop-ups. A send that fails is only added to a count in the server's own log line; the owner sees nothing per member. If the sending key is missing or refused, every run stops quietly with one log line, while the owner believes members were told.
expected: Per message, the owner (or HQ) can see how many phones got the pop-up, how many failed and why, and a missing key raises a visible alert.
how_often: every send that fails, and every send while the key is missing
fix_line: Save each run's sent and failed counts against the message so the panel and HQ can show them

title: A failed nightly purge of 400-day-old AI requests is written only to the server's console
what: The nightly clean-up writes its own record to the HQ audit list first, then runs the purge of old AI requests and of test gyms. If either fails, the only trace is a console line that nobody reads, so the 400-day deletion promise can quietly stop.
expected: The outcome of every nightly purge, including failures, lands in the HQ audit list.
fix_line: Record the purge results in the HQ audit list after they run

title: Owners' mobile numbers are kept forever in plain form to stop repeat free trials, and the privacy notice does not say so
what: When a gym is started with a checked number, that number is saved in plain form in a list used to allow one free trial per number. The list has no deletion rule and outlives the gym. The privacy notice section for owners says only a coded form of the WhatsApp-checked number is kept and does not list this record or how long it is kept.
expected: Keep only a coded form of the number for the trial check, and name it with its keep time in the privacy notice.
proof: code-read (later migrations outside this folder not checked)
how_often: every gym started with a checked number
fix_line: Store a coded form of the number and add the record to the privacy notice

title: Whether a gym pop-up reaches a member depends on phone settings nobody can see
what: A pop-up reaches a member only if the app is installed and linked, 'Messages from my gym' is on, the phone allows the app's notifications and its 'Messages from your gym' channel, and the phone maker's battery rules do not hold back the data message. The owner sees none of these per member.
expected: The owner can see per member whether pop-ups can reach them, and the reachable count is checked on real phones.
how_often: cannot be proven in the cloud, needs a real-phone check (look at: app notification permission, the 'Messages from your gym' channel sound and banner, battery saver on Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo, Samsung with the app closed)
fix_line: Show per member whether pop-ups are on, and test the closed-app pop-up on the main phone makers

title: A workout in progress can vanish on reopening the app with no word to the member
what: When the app reopens, it reads back the workout that was open. If that read fails, if the saved copy is damaged, or if loading the plan's targets for it fails, the workout is simply not reopened. The only trace is a console line; the member sees an empty Workout tab and the sets they logged are gone from view.
expected: The member is told the open workout could not be reopened, and the saved copy is kept so it can be recovered.
how_often: rare: only when the phone's storage read or the targets load fails
fix_line: Show a short message and keep the saved copy when a workout cannot be reopened

title: Tapping several kinds of gym pop-up may open the app without going to the thing it names
what: The server sends pop-ups that point at orders, diet plan, measurements, the gym's reply to a message and MettleUp's help reply. The app's tap handler in this folder knows only the workout, the gym tab, the gym inbox and the trainer-reply page; any other page in a tapped pop-up is ignored, so the member lands wherever the app last was.
expected: Every pop-up the server sends opens the page it talks about.
proof: code-read (another tap handler outside this folder may route these; not checked)
how_often: every tap on an order, diet, measurement, message-reply or help-reply pop-up, if no other handler exists
fix_line: Let the tap handler open any page the pop-up names, with the gym tab as the fallback

title: The panel says 'Members see it now' for today's workout even where members' app hides it
what: After saving today's workout the panel says members see it now. The member app hides the card for a Starter gym, for members with no linked gym, and when a workout is already open. The panel's today's-workout card shows no plan check and no count of who can see it.
expected: The panel says who will see today's workout (or that the gym's plan does not include it) before saying members see it.
proof: code-read (the Starter rule itself lives in a file outside this folder)
who: owners and trainers on a Starter gym, and owners whose members have not linked the app
fix_line: Show the plan limit and the number of members who can see it next to the save

title: Rest-timer alerts depend on phone settings that are checked only on Android
what: The rest alert status row reads the phone's notification, sound and exact-alarm access and offers a fix, but only on Android; elsewhere it never shows. Whether the alert sounds with the screen off also depends on the phone maker's battery rules and on a paired watch.
expected: Rest alerts are proven on real phones and the watch, and any phone where the state cannot be read says so.
how_often: cannot be proven in the cloud, needs a real-phone check (look at: rest alert with screen off on Xiaomi, Samsung, Oppo, Vivo with battery saver on; the alert channel sound; the watch card's 'Rest is over' when the phone is in a pocket)
fix_line: Run the screen-off rest alert check on the main phone makers and the watch
